newsitem.title: PERU: Confusion reigns over deaths in Peru mudslide.
newsitem.headline: Confusion reigns over deaths in Peru mudslide.

text.p: Confusion reigned over the extent of damage caused by a huge mudslide that apparently buried two villages in Peru's southeastern Andean region early on Tuesday.
Some officials said the landslide caused a major disaster with up to 200 people killed, but others insisted inhabitants of the two villages were evacuated in time and none was killed.
The mudslide occurred at around 4 a.m. (0900 GMT) in the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra in the mountainous southeastern region of Apurimac.

Luis Barra Pacheco, mayor of the regional capital Abancay, told Reuters he had travelled to the area and was told by local people that 40 families totalling between 150 and 200 people were buried in the landslide. Seven bodies had been found, he said.
The state news agency Andina quoted local officials as saying about 25 families were buried.
And local police officials told Reuters they had received reports from villagers that 50 to 60 families were buried, with 14 bodies recovered from so far from Ccocha.
However, Peru's Civil Defence service denied there had been any deaths, saying all inhabitants were evacuated from the villages before the landslip.

"By luck, with a cooperation unseen on other occasions, all the entities of Abancay have collaborated and were able to evacuate, with the organisation of the Civil Defence, the 40 families," Civil Defence official Homero Nurena told local television.

The region's deputy governor, Jose Caiyahua, also denied there had been deaths. "It's true there was an avalanche, but it's false that there were any deaths. Only houses and trees have fallen down," Caiyahua told Reuters.
The zone's military head, Col. Manuel Montesinos, also said no one died. He said he had visited the zone, and "there is no injury at all, or deaths."
All the reports claiming people had died were based on second-hand reports from villagers in the area.
Barra Pacheco said an estimated 300,000 cubic meters (10.5 million cubic feet) of mud slid off a nearby mountain and buried the two communities.
"Two villages have totally disappeared. We're talking about 150 to 200 people buried," he told Reuters in a telephone interview, adding seven bodies had been recovered.
Local radio station Radioprogramas del Peru read a list of more than 70 names of people it said were missing after the mudslide.
